messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: BMC firmware v2026.03.17 applied to racks: rwk-03, rwk-07, rwk-11 in us-west3 — rollout window 02:10-02:18 UTC

maya: seeing a bunch of provisioning failures in us-west3 since ~02:22. GPU nodes failing healthchecks and stuck in PROVISIONING.

ryan: I’m seeing oob network DHCP pool exhausted on the management VLAN for those racks. dhcpd logs show lots of renew failures and repeated DISCOVER floods.

alex: can you paste a sample log?

ryan: here are tail lines from the jump host:

```
Mar 17 02:21:58 dhcpd[4123]: DHCPDISCOVER from 00:1a:4b:xx:xx:xx via br-oob
Mar 17 02:21:58 dhcpd[4123]: DHCPOFFER to 10.200.3.45 from 10.200.3.1
Mar 17 02:21:59 dhcpd[4123]: DHCPREQUEST from 00:1a:4b:xx:xx:xx via br-oob
Mar 17 02:21:59 dhcpd[4123]: DHCPACK on 10.200.3.45 to 00:1a:4b:xx:xx:xx
Mar 17 02:22:01 dhcpd[4123]: DHCPDISCOVER from 00:1a:4b:yy:yy:yy via br-oob
Mar 17 02:22:01 dhcpd[4123]: no free leases
```
\nryan: DHCP table at 100% and churn rate spiked after the firmware rollout.

maya: impact: provisioning API retries increased ~8x, capacity for hosted GPUs in us-west3 dropped by ~14% while instances stuck. Cost spike on retries and API calls.

ops-bot: flagged: alert ingested — oob-dhcp-pool-exhaustion (severity: high)

oncall-bot: assigned to @ryan (oncall).

ryan: started mitigations: bumped dhcp lease time temporarily and evicted stale leases for known asset MAC prefix. command run: `sudo dhcp-lease-list --leasefile /var/lib/dhcp/dhcpd.leases | grep rwk-`

alex: can we isolate the BMCs from broadcast storms? Maybe the new fw introduced a gratuitous DHCP-client behaviour on some BMC models.

sophia: confirmed with hw-inventory: rwk-07 uses BMC model AST2600 and versions that were in the rollout. AST2600 has a known regression with DHCP renews in v2026.03.X in vendor notes.

maya: tagging the firmware team — @alex please coordinate rollback or vendor hotfix. We need to restore capacity for Dedicated customers ASAP.

alex: proposed short-term plan:
1) roll back BMC fw on rwk-03 and rwk-07 (rwk-11 seems healthy)
2) add static leases for jump hosts and provisioner-control IPs on br-oob
3) throttle provisioner concurrency for us-west3 to reduce retry storm
4) open vendor SR for AST2600 DHCP regression

ryan: implementing 2 and 3 now. throttling set in provisioner: `--concurrency=6` for us-west3.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued: bmc-fw-rollback v2026.02.10 -> targets [rwk-03, rwk-07] — ETA 02:48 UTC

maya: notify a couple Dedicated customers on us-west3 about degraded capacity and potential cold starts.

sophia: running cold-reset on suspect BMCs as intermediate measure: `for id in rwk-03 rwk-07; do ipmitool -H bmc-$id -I lanplus -U admin -P **** mc reset cold; done`

alex: also adding temporary static mapping entries for provisioner-control and jump hosts to keep them out of DHCP churn:

```
10.200.3.5  aa:bb:cc:11:22:33  # provisioner-1
10.200.3.6  aa:bb:cc:11:22:34  # jump-usw3
```
\nryan: eviction and static entries in place, provisioner concurrency reduced. retry rate halved, capacity recovering slowly.

deploy-bot: rollback started at 02:47 UTC (bmc-fw-rollback job id bfw-2026-9084).

ops-bot: note: provisioning retries generated ~89k extra API calls and ~420GB of control-plane egress in the window — preliminary cost estimate: ~$1.5k for the incident window.

maya: good work on the quick mitigations. @alex follow up with vendor and schedule a controlled re-roll after vendor patch. We should also add a preflight DHCP churn test to the rollout playbook.

deploy-bot: rollback completed at 03:10 UTC — bmc-fw v2026.02.10 restored on rwk-03 and rwk-07. healthchecks passing.

ryan: dhcp pool stabilized, provisioning resumed, hosted GPU capacity back to normal in us-west3. Monitoring green.

sophia: creating incident ticket and postmortem stub. Action items: vendor SR, rollout preflight, static-lease fallbacks, firmware pinning for AST2600.

maya: thanks everyone. we'll run a short after-action meeting at 11:00 UTC to capture details. :thumbsup:
